checks: Between consecutive vertex heights, a crossed original face is identified by strict inequalities between its minimum and maximum height and intersects the section in dimension one lower. The section face incidence and edge-vertex labels are fixed on that interval.

A single pulling order therefore gives the same simplices throughout the interval. Their translated vertices are affine in height and their nonzero determinant signs are constant, giving section-area degree at most d−1 and cap degree at most d by Fubini.

Projected compactness and interpolation with interior points show both proper-side area limits, and the single body-side limit at a supporting facet. A lower-dimensional supporting face gives zero area by the shrinking projected neighborhood bound.

The branch sign for q≠0 is selected by the first jet; when q=0 the acceleration selects the side and D(r) is the correct second coefficient. For d=1, an endpoint facet has counting area one and the clipped interval directly gives both signs.

For an exact calibration, the triangle with vertices (0,0),(1,0),(0,1) has F(T)=(1−T)^2/2 for 0≤T≤1 and constant continuation on either side. Its knot at zero has one inside derivative −1 and one outside derivative 0, and its outside-support vertex at one has first derivative zero but nonzero body-side second derivative.
